concepts.title: Laws of Chemical Combination
concepts.definition: Chemical reactions obey fixed rules: the law of conservation of mass keeps the total mass of reactants and products equal, and the law of constant proportions keeps the elements of a compound in one fixed ratio by mass in every sample.
concepts.key_idea: Mass is never lost and ratios never drift: two laws that anchor all chemistry.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc109.txt sections on laws of chemical combination

solution_steps.explain: Conservation of mass demands equal totals on both sides.
Constant proportions demands the same element ratio in every sample.
Atoms rearrange without loss, which secures both laws.

concepts.title: Atoms, Molecules and Ions
concepts.definition: An atom is the smallest particle of an element, a molecule is a group of atoms bonded together - like the two-atom molecules of oxygen and hydrogen - and charged species called ions, cations and anions, arise when atoms gain or lose electrons.
concepts.key_idea: Atoms build molecules; gaining or losing electrons turns them into ions.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc109.txt sections on atoms, molecules and ions

solution_steps.explain: Decide whether the species is a single atom, a molecule or an ion.
Atomicity counts atoms per molecule, as 2 for oxygen.
Electron loss gives cations, electron gain gives anions.

concepts.title: Writing Chemical Formulae
concepts.definition: Chemical formulae are written by the valency criss-cross method: the valencies of the ions or atoms swap places as subscripts, so the formula carries the fixed ratio in which the elements combine - as in water, H2O.
concepts.key_idea: Valencies cross over to become subscripts - the charge balance writes the formula.

concepts.title: Atomic Mass, Molecular Mass and the Mole Idea
concepts.definition: Atoms are weighed on a relative scale where carbon-12 sets the unit: atomic masses combine to give molecular mass, and the mole links this invisible scale to grams - one mole containing 6.022 times 10 to the 23 particles.
concepts.key_idea: The mole is chemistry's dozen: Avogadro's number of particles weighs the molecular mass in grams.
